summary: Appomattox County, VA steel tower built 1938 (sources differ on builder and height); last staffed until June 2022; privately owned, visits by appointment; owner plans restoration.

facts.design: 80-foot steel tower with 7-by-7-foot cab (NHLR); a 2026 news report gives 88 feet

access.note: Privately owned. The register says visits are by appointment only, as of 2025, and names Krissy Reynolds as the contact to arrange one. A 2020 blog post describes crossing private property that had a No Trespassing sign.

facts.agency: Private owner (NHLR). The register says the Virginia Division of Forestry constructed it; the Forest Lookouts index lists the Virginia Department of Forestry.

events.note: Register description says constructed by the Virginia Division of Forestry in 1938; the register's Built field says 1939; a 2026 news report says the Civilian Conservation Corps built it
Last employee, a former forester who climbed the tower's 109 stairs for 33 years, retired June 2022

corrections.proposed: 1938 built (register description; the register's Built field says 1939)
corrections.why: The register's own description and the 2026 news report both give 1938. The 1939 figure comes only from the register's Built field.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register describes an 80-foot steel tower; a 2026 news report gives 88 feet. The story reports both and does not choose.

The register description says 1938 and the Virginia Division of Forestry; its Built field says 1939; the news report says the Civilian Conservation Corps built it in 1938. The story reports the disagreement.

The register lists a private owner; the Forest Lookouts index lists the Virginia Department of Forestry against the tower. The story calls the tower privately owned now and names the forestry division as its historic builder.

notes_for_editor: The register withholds coordinates at the owner's request, but our record carries lat/lon 37.43541, -78.80471 from the FFLA index. Please decide whether to keep them public. The owner is named in the news report; the story does not name him and omits the register's contact email. The register's nominator (Ricky Butler) and the news report's former forester (Rick Butler) may be the same person; the story does not link them. A 2020 blog says about a dozen towers remain in Virginia while WTVR says about 50; no count is used. Visits are by appointment only; the register names Krissy Reynolds as the contact, so the story sends readers to her and does not name the owner or print the contact email.
